content: his dispute involved a building under construction and life insurance policies. The wife claimed the building was funded primarily with her personal money, arguing against equal shares. The Court reinforced the principle that the legal community (Art. 194 CC) is distinct from ordinary co-ownership; shares are strictly equal and cannot be modified by proving different financial inputs. Regarding the insurance, it established that "case of life" policies where the policyholder is the beneficiary are personal assets, while policies intended as indirect donations to the other spouse are excluded from the community under Art. 179(b) CC.
